runs.t: This document replaces Chapter 19 of Todd Lammle, CCNA Certification Study Guide, Volume 2, Exam 200-301 (2020), book pages 549 to 594 (PDF pages 607 to 651). It follows the book's order, keeps its learning objectives, and adds plain-English explanations, worked numbers, labs and questions. Every difference from the book is tagged.

Which two encryption methods are based on RC4?
WEP and TKIP - AES-CCMP replaced RC4.
What does the four-way handshake produce?

Which WPA3 feature stops offline dictionary attacks?

What does OWE give an open network?

These 28 questions are original. Also do the book's own 20 review questions (pages 590 to 593) and check them in the book's Appendix. Answer on paper first.
Which 2.4 GHz channels are non-overlapping in the United States?
B - Script check: only 1, 6, 11 fit in channels 1 to 11.
Which frequency bands do 802.11a, 802.11b and 802.11g use?
a: 5 GHz; b: 2.4 GHz; g: 2.4 GHz - Book review questions 2 to 4.
Which statement about the 5 GHz band is true compared with 2.4 GHz?
A. Longer range and fewer channels
B. Shorter range and more non-overlapping channels
C. The same range and the same channels
D. Longer range and more channels
B - Higher frequency travels less far but gives more usable channels.
What is an SSID, and what is its maximum length?
The name of a wireless network; up to 32 octets - It is not the same as a BSSID (the AP radio's MAC).
An AP is installed on the ceiling. At minimum, which parameter must be configured so a client can use it?
C - Open authentication needs only the SSID (book question 5).
Two APs share the SSID Sales and are connected by the wired network. What is this?
An ESS (extended service set) - A single AP and its clients is a BSS.
Two laptops connect directly with no AP. What is it called?
C - Independent basic service set (ad hoc).
A repeater AP is added. What happens to throughput in the repeated area?
It drops by about half - Use repeaters for low-bandwidth devices only.
True or false: two non-root bridges can talk to each other in general.
False - Exception: a repeater-style non-root bridge that has a root bridge in its uplink.
Reflected signals arrive 180 degrees out of phase with the main signal. What is the name of the effect?
Nulling - Reflection causes multipath; 120 to 170 degrees is downfade; 360 is upfade.
A signal bends around a building and leaves a dead spot. Which behavior is this?
B - Diffraction bends around; refraction bends through different media.
Which signal is stronger: -45 dBm or -85 dBm?
-45 dBm - Closer to zero is stronger.
Roughly what does +3 dB do to the power?
Doubles it - -3 dB halves it; +10 dB multiplies by 10 (script checked).
How much of the Fresnel zone must be clear?
At least 60 percent - Even with perfect visual line of sight.
Does a higher SNR mean a better or a worse link?
Better - More signal compared with noise.
Which authentication type uses a challenge text encrypted with a WEP key?
Shared-key authentication - It is insecure and not used.
Which two encryption methods are based on RC4?
B - SAE is the WPA3-Personal handshake.
In WPA2-Enterprise, which key exists before the four-way handshake, and which key does the handshake produce?
PMK before; PTK from the handshake - The handshake uses ANonce and SNonce.
Which WPA3 feature gives built-in resistance to offline dictionary attacks?
Which WPA3 enhancement replaces plain open authentication and gives each device its own key?
OWE (Opportunistic Wireless Encryption) - Not "OWL", a made-up distractor.
Which feature must all WPA3 networks use for management frames?
Protected Management Frames (PMF) - Required in WPA3.
Choose two statements that describe WPA.
A. Dynamic encryption keys change during the connection
B. All devices must use the same static key
C. It can use PSK authentication
D. Static WEP keys are required
Why would an administrator create several SSIDs on one AP?
To give different groups different security settings - It does not add speed.
What three things make roaming work well inside a building?
Same SSID and security on the APs, different channels on neighbors, 15 to 20 percent cell overlap - The book gives 20 percent in text and 15 percent in a question.
A client with a b/g card cannot join an 802.11b/g AP, and the AP lists no clients at all. What is a likely reason?
A. Wrong channel set on the client
D. Wrong SSID on the client
D - The AP only lists clients that associate. A wrong IP or key would still show an association attempt. A client usually scans all channels itself.
Name three common causes of Wi-Fi interference.
Other APs on the same or adjacent channel, microwave ovens, Bluetooth and cordless phones - v2.0 objective 1.5.d.
Is hiding the SSID a real security measure?
No - The name still appears in some frames; use encryption instead.
Extension of Ethernet. Half-duplex, shared channel. AP bridges wireless to wired (the DS).
Autonomous (configured alone) or lightweight (managed by a WLC; CAPWAP).
IBSS = no AP. BSS = one AP. ESS = several APs, same SSID. Repeater halves throughput. Bridges: root and non-root.
Network name, 1 to 32 octets. BSSID = AP radio MAC. Multiple SSIDs = different security, not more speed.

20 MHz apart, non-overlapping. UNII-1 36 to 48, UNII-2 52 to 64, UNII-3 149 to 161 (also 100 to 144 and 165).

Absorption (weaker through objects), reflection (bounces), multipath (late copies), refraction (bends in different media), diffraction (around objects), scattering (many directions).
dBm relative to 1 mW. Closer to zero is stronger. +3 dB doubles, +10 dB x10.
Keep at least 60 percent clear. RF line of sight, not just visual.
RSSI = signal strength. SNR = signal vs noise; higher is better.
Open (SSID only, Layer 2) or shared-key (WEP challenge, insecure).
WEP and TKIP = RC4. WPA = TKIP/MIC. WPA2 = AES-CCMP. WPA3 = SAE (Personal), GCMP-256 (192-bit mode), OWE for open networks, PMF required.
PMK, then four-way handshake, then PTK (with ANonce and SNonce).
Personal = PSK or SAE. Enterprise = 802.1X / EAP with RADIUS.
